text:
Thoughts
expand_more
As established in previous turns, this source contains no substantive discussions of any of the twelve B001 passage comparisons (e.g., Romans 4:3 / Gen 15:6, Romans 9:25–26 / Hos 1–2, Galatians 3:13 / Deut 21:23). The volume is a critical edition of the Greek New Testament text with a variant-recording apparatus, rather than an exegetical commentary or study of Old Testament citations. Consequently, no footnotes or bibliographic entries in the source address these specific intertextual comparisons or their citation problems.
However, the editor explicitly cites and interacts with a specific corpus of scholarly editions and studies in the introduction, footnotes, and apparatus to establish the text and resolve textual problems across the New Testament (including the Pauline epistles). The relevant sources visible in the text and notes are detailed below:
Sources Cited in Footnotes and Introduction Regarding Text-Critical Problems
1. Bruce M. Metzger
Title: A Textual Commentary on The Greek New Testament
1
2
Publication Year: 1971
1
2
Pages: Page 616
1
2
Locator: Page xii, Footnote 10
1
2
Why It Matters: Cited regarding breathing marks on pronouns as exegetical decisions rather than purely lexical ones
1
2
. Specifically, Holmes follows a minority position of the UBS Editorial Committee discussed on page 616 of Metzger's first edition (discussing Philippians 3:21, a note omitted from the second edition) to print rough breathings on forms of αὐτός when reflexive meaning is intended
1
2
.
2. David C. Parker
Title: “The Development of the Critical Text of the Epistle of James: From Lachmann to the Editio Critica Maior” (in New Testament Textual Criticism and Exegesis: Festschrift J. Delobel, ed. A. Denaux; BETL 161; Leuven: Leuven University Press and Peeters)
3
4
Publication Year: 2002
3
4
Pages: Page 325 and Page 329
3
more_horiz
Locator: Page x, Footnote 3; Page xiv–xv, Footnote 16
3
more_horiz
Why It Matters:
On page x, Parker is cited (p. 329) for commending Tregelles's "consistency of view and breadth of appreciation" of textual evidence over against the tendency of Westcott–Hort, Tischendorf, and Lachmann to become preoccupied with a single "big discovery" (such as Vaticanus or Sinaiticus)
3
4
.
On page xiv–xv, Parker is cited (p. 325) regarding the concept of "wise reticence" in the face of difficult textual choices
5
6
. Holmes explains why he restricts single square brackets to only six instances in the New Testament (including Ephesians 1:1 and Colossians 1:20), arguing that brackets have been overused to evade difficult editorial decisions and introduce an inherent bias toward inclusion
5
.
3. Brooke Foss Westcott and Fenton John Anthony Hort
Title: The New Testament in the Original Greek, vol. 1: Text; vol. 2: Introduction [and] Appendix
7
8
Publication Year: 1881
7
8
Pages: UNKNOWN (entire edition utilized)
7
8
Locator: Pages ix, xi, xiii, xiv, xv, xviii
2
more_horiz
Why It Matters: Served as the initial baseline and starting point for the SBLGNT
9
. After orthographic adjustments, its text was collated against the other three primary editions
9
. It also provides the standard for punctuation, elision, crasis, movable ν, and the apparatus's recording of ancient non-original text preserved in double brackets (〚WH〛)
2
more_horiz
.
4. Samuel Prideaux Tregelles
Title: The Greek New Testament, Edited from Ancient Authorities, with their Various Readings in Full, and the Latin Version of Jerome
7
more_horiz
Publication Year: 1857–1879
7
more_horiz
Pages: UNKNOWN (entire edition utilized)
7
more_horiz
Locator: Pages ix–x, xi, xv, xviii
3
more_horiz
Why It Matters: One of the four primary reference editions collated for every variation unit
5
more_horiz
. It provides a balanced nineteenth-century critical alternative to Westcott and Hort that does not over-privilege Codex Vaticanus
3
4
.
5. Richard J. Goodrich and Albert L. Lukaszewski
Title: A Reader’s Greek New Testament
14
15
Publication Year: 2003 (with reference to a 2nd edition in 2007 modified by Gordon Fee)
4
14
Pages: Page 10, Footnote 6
4
Locator: Page x, Footnotes 5–6; Pages xi, xv, xvii
4
more_horiz
Why It Matters: One of the four primary reference editions collated across all 6,928 variation units
5
more_horiz
. It presents the Greek text underlying the New International Version (reconstructed by Edward Goodrick and John Kohlenberger III), embodying modern editorial decisions of the Committee on Bible Translation
4
14
.
6. Maurice A. Robinson and William G. Pierpont
Title: The New Testament in the Original Greek: Byzantine Textform 2005
4
more_horiz
Publication Year: 2005
4
more_horiz
Pages: UNKNOWN (entire edition utilized)
4
more_horiz
Locator: Pages x–xi, xv, xvii
4
more_horiz
Why It Matters: One of the four primary reference editions
4
more_horiz
. It serves as the primary witness for the Byzantine textual tradition in the collation process, ensuring systematic comparison between Byzantine and critical/Alexandrian readings
5
9
.
7. Kurt Aland, Matthew Black, Bruce M. Metzger, Allen Wikgren, and Eberhard Nestle
Titles:
The Greek New Testament (UBS)
3
13
Novum Testamentum Graece (Nestle-Aland / NA26–27)
13
15
The Text of the New Testament (Kurt Aland and Barbara Aland, 2nd ed., trans. E. F. Rhodes, 1989)
13
Publication Years: 1898, 1936, 1966, 1989
3
13
Pages: Page v (UBS 1966); p. 38* (Nestle 16th ed., 1936); pp. 19–20 (Aland & Aland 1989)
3
13
Locator: Page ix, Footnotes 1–2; Page xvii
3
more_horiz
Why It Matters: Represents the contemporary "standard text"
17
18
. Holmes establishes SBLGNT to challenge the passive acceptance of NA/UBS as a "final" text, noting that SBLGNT departs from it in more than 540 variation units
18
19
. NA is also cited explicitly in the apparatus whenever it differs from the NIV text
5
15
.
8. Barbara Aland, Kurt Aland, Gerd Mink, Holger Strutwolf, and Klaus Wachtel (INTF)
Title: Novum Testamentum Graecum: Editio Critica Maior, vol. 4: Catholic Letters (4 installments)
20
more_horiz
Publication Year: 1997–2005
20
22
Pages: Page 24* (in installment 2, The Letters of Peter)
22
Locator: Page xvi–xvii; Appendix, Pages 515–516
20
more_horiz
Why It Matters: Cited in the Appendix to compare the text of the Catholic Letters, documenting 39 variation units where SBLGNT differs from the ECM
21
23
. Footnote 1 (p. 515) cites page 24* of the Peter installment regarding the ECM's system of bold dots signaling readings of equal value or high doubt
22
.
9. Frederick William Danker and Walter Bauer
Title: A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament and Other Early Christian Literature (BDAG, 3rd ed.)
1
more_horiz
Publication Year: 2000
24
Pages: Mention of entry §21 in F. Blass, A. Debrunner, and R. W. Funk (BDF)
24
Locator: Pages xii–xiii, Footnote 11
1
more_horiz
Why It Matters: Governs the orthography, accentuation, and breathings of both the printed text and the textual apparatus, resolving spelling discrepancies across older editions (with rare noted exceptions like Colossians 2:16)
1
more_horiz
.
10. Michael W. Holmes
Titles:
“Reconstructing the Text of the New Testament” (in The Blackwell Companion to the New Testament, ed. David E. Aune; Oxford: Wiley-Blackwell)
9
25
The Apostolic Fathers: Greek Texts and English Translations (3rd ed.; Grand Rapids: Baker Academic)
5
more_horiz
Publication Years: 2007 (Apostolic Fathers), 2010 (Blackwell)
10
more_horiz
Pages: Pages 77–89 (Blackwell)
25
Locator: Page xi, Footnote 7; Page xiii, Footnote 12; Page xv, Footnote 17
5
more_horiz
Why It Matters: Provides the external statement of the editor's text-critical methodology (Blackwell) and supplies the model for capitalization rules and apparatus formatting (Apostolic Fathers)
5
more_horiz
.
🔍 Would you like to review how any specific variation units in the Pauline epistles—such as Romans 4:1–2, 1 Corinthians 12:10, or Galatians 3:19—are treated in the apparatus against these cited editions?
